source.title: Holomorphic mappings: Survey of some results and discussion of open problems

accepted.question_text: Let f: C^2 -> C^2 be an entire holomorphic mapping. Must the Euclidean volume of the image f(C^2), measured in the usual Euclidean volume on C^2, be infinite?

Let D be a divisor in complex projective space P^n with normal crossings, meaning that D is a sum of distinct smooth irreducible hypersurfaces with multiplicity one and, at each point, the local defining equations of the components through that point form part of a holomorphic coordinate system. In terms of deg(D), the total degree of D, and #(D), the number of components of D, what conditions ensure that every holomorphic mapping f: C^m -> P^n \ D is necessarily constant?
Let D be a normal-crossings divisor in P^n, and let f: C -> P^n \ D be a holomorphic curve whose image misses D. If deg(D) is at least n+2, must the image f(C) lie in an algebraic subvariety of P^n?

Let f: C^m -> P^n be a holomorphic mapping. Let |D| be the complete linear system of divisors of degree d in P^n, and let D_1,...,D_t be smooth divisors in |D| such that D_1+...+D_t has normal crossings. Assume f(C^m) is not contained in any divisor in |D|. For the Nevanlinna defects delta(D_j), defined from the counting function N(D,r) and order function T(r) by delta(D)=1-limsup_{r->infinity} N(D,r)/T(r), is sum_{j=1}^t delta(D_j) <= (n+1)/d?

Can one define a subclass of holomorphic mappings f: C^m -> P^n that gives a reasonable geometric and analytic value-distribution theory in higher codimension: every map in the subclass should satisfy the Nevanlinna inequality N(D,r) <= T(r)+O(1), the Liouville-type relation integral over D in |D| of delta(D) dmu(D)=0 for divisors in a complete linear system, and the functorial restriction property that f restricted to C^k remains in the subclass whenever f:C^m -> P^n is in the subclass?

Let V be a smooth projective variety with canonical bundle K_V and let L be a positive line bundle. Let D_1,...,D_t be smooth divisors in the complete linear system |L| such that D_1+...+D_t has normal crossings. Suppose f:C -> V is a holomorphic curve whose image is not contained in any divisor in |L+K_V|. With Nevanlinna defects delta(D_j) and the Chern-class comparison notation in which lambda > [alpha/beta] means lambda beta - alpha is represented by a positive definite (1,1)-form, is sum_{j=1}^t delta(D_j) <= [c_1(K_V)/c_1(L)]?
Let V be an algebraic surface with positive canonical bundle, and let f:C -> V be a holomorphic mapping. Must the image f(C) lie in an algebraic curve in V?
accepted.context_brief: curves on surfaces of general type

accepted.question_text: For an algebraic surface V with positive canonical bundle, are there only finitely many rational maps f:C -> V having distinct images?

For a general holomorphic mapping f:C -> V from the complex line to an abelian variety V, and for a positive divisor D on V, must the image f(C) intersect D? The question excludes relying on the special case where f is a group homomorphism.
Let V be an n-dimensional complex torus and let f:C^n -> V be a nondegenerate holomorphic mapping. Must the image f(C^n) be dense in V?
